I extracted and abstracted another part from #767 but this time it is way more elementary: If the number of elements reachable from an element a along a relation r is at most k, then any of those elements can be reached in at most k - 1 steps.

This result and the formalism developed starting from there should be useful for many computation models that have a concept of "step". It has a result that for relations that can be applied to computations to obtain that if a configuration is re-visited during a (nondeterministic) computation, that loop can be cut from it.

Two main questions mainly concerning the concept of "Path" are if we 1) want to rather adopt a similar definition from Mathlib (see the PR) even if it requires conversion back and forth and 2) would rather use a different name than "Path".

:light_bulb:

Ok, this pull request has some nice history now ;)
Github currently throws some unicorns at me, so I cannot update the description.
I defined a List.IsChainFromTo structure which is List.IsChain plus designated start and end elements. It has a theorem that say that if the list has a duplicate, then a shorter version exists. I will try to upstream this into mathlib.
This is then in turn applied in the RelatesInSteps.lean file to show that if b is reachable from a along the relation r, then it is reachable in fewer steps than there are elements reachable from a.

Thanks for the detailed reviews so far, @Thomas Waring and @Ching-Tsun Chou ! I would like to discuss where this pull request is heading and if it's a good idea to introduce List.IsChainFromTo.
Since the results in that PR are useful for graph theory and reasoning in the configuration graph of nondeterministic Turing machines (and maybe other machines), I would like to check if basing it on List.IsChain is really the best choice. Of course, a List.IsChainFromTo is a good way to formalize a walk / path inside a directed graph. Another choice would be RelSeries in Mathlib/Order.
The advantage of RelSeries over a plain List.IsChain is that it has a nonemptyness assumption. So instead of List.IsChainFromTo, we could use RelSeries and directly access head and last.
When using RelSeries, the main lemma in that PR would be changed from

lemma List.IsChainFromTo.exists_length_lt_of_not_nodup
    (hc : chain.IsChainFromTo r a b)
    (h_dup : ¬ chain.Nodup) :
    ∃ chain' : List α, chain'.IsChainFromTo r a b ∧ chain'.length < chain.length := by

to

lemma RelSeries.exists_length_lt_of_not_nodup
    (s : RelSeries r)
    (h_dup : ¬ s.toList.Nodup) :
    ∃ s' : RelSeries r, s'.head = s.head ∧ s'.last = s.last ∧ s'.length < s.length := by

Most of the lemmas we would add for IsChainFromTo already exist for RelSeries. It has an induction principle, snoc, cons, append, smash, reverse, etc.

So what are the opinions? Should we add a new type or base this on top of RelSeries?
And there is LTS.Execution. If the identity of the transition label is erased, LTS.Execution reduces to List.IsChainFromTo.

i'm inclined to say stick with IsChain(FromTo) — note that a nonempty version of the former used to be in mathlib and was deprecated. my reasoning

  • RelSeries uses SetRel not α → α → Prop, so wouldn't mesh with the rest of the library — including LTS.Execution as @Ching-Tsun Chou mentioned, but also RelatesInSteps which was the origin of this pr iirc
  • i think a structure based on List α rather than Fin n → α matches better with the rest of the library, too
  • for me a big part of the appeal of IsChainFromTo is that it packages the head and getLast assumptions, which SetRel doesn't, so we might need a new definition anyway
  • the lemmas you mention for SetRel also exist for List.IsChain, and imo lifting them to IsChainFromTo is not too hard — i think i mentioned in review but if this pr is blocking something else i don't mind adding those api lemmas in a follow-up (subject ofc to the opinion of others)

i agree that carrying around all the various List.head? calls and ≠ [] assumptions etc can be a bit of a headache, but it doesn't seem insurmountable to me.
The fact that the nonempty version was deprecated does not sound good for our chances of upstreaming.
It also seems that RelSeries is almost not used in mathlib

the old version packaged the head of the list explicitly, something like List.IsChain' r a l which was changed to List.IsChain r (a :: l) — i think the problem was that it was an entirely separate inductive definition, which ours isn't. in any case i'm not sure we need to upstream for this to be useful
